# Education in Greece
Education in Greece is structured into distinct levels: compulsory preschool (pre-kindergarten and kindergarten, ages 4–6), primary school (six years), and secondary education, which includes lower secondary (Gymnasium, three years, compulsory until age 15) and upper secondary (Lyceum, three years, non-compulsory). Throughout all school years, students progressively study subjects ranging from Modern and Ancient Greek, mathematics, sciences, English and another foreign language, history, IT, physical education, and more. Secondary education features diverse types of schools, such as general, vocational, experimental, and model schools, each with varied curricula and entrance requirements. Progression to higher education depends on obtaining the appropriate school certificates and passing nationwide Pan-Hellenic Examinations.
Vocational pathways are well developed, with Vocational Lyceums (EPAL), Schools of Advanced Vocational Training (SAEK), and vocational schools (EPAS, ESK, PEPAS) offering specialized tracks in fields like engineering, healthcare, IT, agriculture, maritime, tourism, and the arts. Graduates receive diplomas in vocational education corresponding to HQF levels 3–5 and may undergo apprenticeships integrating classroom learning with workplace experience. Tertiary education is primarily provided by public Higher Education Institutions (HEIs)—universities and academies—though a recent law now permits recognized private HEIs. Greek public universities are mostly tuition-free and have begun offering some English-taught programmes, while private colleges tend to provide foreign-accredited degrees. Beyond formal education, Greece supports non-formal and lifelong learning through open courses, digital academies, and specialized vocational centers.
